title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
prompt:
Return the `k`-th smallest value in a BST (1-indexed).

**Example**: `root = [3,1,4,null,2]`, `k = 1` → `1`.

An in-order traversal of a BST visits values in ascending order — stop at the k-th one.
hints: In-order traversal (left, node, right) yields BST values in sorted order.
An iterative in-order uses an explicit stack: push all left descendants, pop, then go right.
Decrement k on each popped node; when it reaches 0 you've found the answer.

solution.explanation: In-order over a BST is ascending, so the k-th node visited is the k-th smallest — and the iterative stack lets us stop early, giving O(height + k) instead of traversing the whole tree.
